explain.say: A hummingbird's heart can beat about 1,200 times a minute in flight, while an elephant's beats about 30 times. In general, the smaller the animal, the faster its heart.

explain.say: Small animals have a lot of skin for their size, so they lose body heat quickly. To stay warm they burn food fast, and every cell needs a quick supply of oxygen.

explain.say: A fast heartbeat delivers that oxygen. A cat's heart beats about 130 times a minute and yours about 70, while a horse's beats about 35.

explain.say: Big animals keep heat well and burn food more slowly for their size, so a slow, powerful heartbeat is enough. An elephant's huge heart beats about 30 times a minute.

faq.q: Why does a tiny animal's heart beat so fast?
faq.a: Small bodies lose heat quickly because they have lots of surface for their volume. To stay warm, small animals burn food fast, and their hearts beat fast to deliver the oxygen their cells need.
asks: Why does a mouse's heart beat so fast?
What is surface area to volume ratio?

faq.q: Which animal has the slowest heartbeat?
faq.a: Large whales do. A blue whale's heart beats a few times a minute while diving, sometimes only about twice, and an elephant's resting heart beats about 30 times a minute.
asks: Do big animals have slower hearts?
How slow is an elephant's heart?

faq.q: Do all animals get about the same number of heartbeats in a life?
faq.a: Many mammals get very roughly a billion heartbeats in a lifetime: small ones live fast and die young, big ones beat slowly and live longer. It is a rough pattern, and humans get more than that.
asks: Do animals with fast hearts live shorter lives?
How many times does a heart beat in a lifetime?

faq.q: Why do children have faster heartbeats than adults?
faq.a: Children are smaller, so like small animals they lose heat faster and their bodies are growing, which needs energy. A baby's heart may beat over 100 times a minute.
asks: Why is a baby's heartbeat fast?
Does heart rate slow as you grow?

faq.q: How fast does a mouse's heart beat?
faq.a: A resting mouse's heart beats about 500 to 600 times a minute, around eight times faster than yours.
asks: What is a mouse's heart rate?
Which mammal has the fastest heartbeat?

facts: Smaller mammals and birds generally have faster resting heart rates than larger ones.
A resting mouse's heart beats about 500 to 600 times per minute.

quiz.say: Why does a small animal need a faster heartbeat than a big one?
quiz.show: Small animals need faster hearts because…

options.show: They lose heat faster and burn food faster
options.say: They lose heat faster and burn food faster

options.show: Their hearts are made of different muscle
options.say: Their hearts are made of different muscle

quiz.why: More surface for their size means more heat lost, so they burn fuel and need oxygen faster.

wrong.1: Heart muscle is much the same; the need for oxygen differs.
wrong.2: Even at rest, small animals have fast heartbeats.
